chapter_title: Designing an A/B Test with Students
learning_objective: The learner will examine eight test setups and decide whether a confounding variable is present and, if so, name its source, with at least 7 of 8 setups fully correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** confounder-finder
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** examine
**Learning Objective:** The learner will examine eight test setups and decide whether a confounding variable is present and, if so, name its source, with at least 7 of 8 setups fully correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Confounding Variable, Control Group, Treatment Group, Random Assignment (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each setup the learner chooses Confounder present or No confounder, and when a confounder is present picks its source from the list. A setup is fully correct when the choice and the source both match the Content table. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 setups fully correct on the first attempt. Reading the confounder table is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A large sample removes a confounder. (2) Random assignment is unnecessary when the groups look alike. (3) A confounder always makes the improved version look better. **Instructional Rationale:** Examining a setup for a second difference between groups is an Analyze-level action. Setups that differ in one way each, and two with no confounder, teach the learner to name the difference and to know when to stop looking. **Content:** The two choices: Confounder present, No confounder. The sources: Teacher, Time of day, Extra help, Different tests, Student choice, Different period of the year. The eight setups (all made up): | # | Setup | Correct choice | Source | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | The morning section uses the original, and the afternoon section uses the improved version. | Confounder present | Time of day | Alertness and the students in each section differ, so the version is not the only difference. | | 2 | One teacher teaches both groups with the same script in the same week, students are assigned by random number, and both groups take the same test. | No confounder | None | The groups differ only in version. | | 3 | The treatment group also gets a 10-minute review before the post-test. | Confounder present | Extra help | The review is a second difference. | | 4 | The control group is tested in September and the treatment group in March. | Confounder present | Different period of the year | Students learn more in the intervening months. | | 5 | Students choose which version to use. | Confounder present | Student choice | Motivated students may choose the new version. | | 6 | The improved version is taught by a teacher who is excited about it, and the original by a teacher who is not. | Confounder present | Teacher | The teacher's attitude is a second difference. | | 7 | The treatment group takes the resource's own quiz as the post-test, and the control group takes a separate test. | Confounder present | Different tests | The groups are measured differently. | | 8 | Both groups use their version for the same time, in the same room, with the same instructions, and a coin flip assigns each student. | No confounder | None | The groups differ only in version. | **Provenance:** The setups are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The sources follow the chapter section "Confounding Variable". **Rules:** Each setup has exactly one correct choice. Six have a confounder and two do not. Each of the six sources appears once. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one setup. 2. The learner chooses Confounder present or No confounder. If a confounder is present, the learner also picks the source. 3. The sim shows whether the choice and the source were correct, and the Why text. 4. After setup 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 setups in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [choice], [source]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The answer is [choice], [source]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can find what else is different." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed setup. **Starting State:** The first setup in the shuffled order and the two choices. The question shown is "Is anything besides the version different between the groups?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's table of confounders lists teacher, time of day, extra help, different tests, and student choice. The sim adds a different period of the year.
